target_customer: Nigerian retail crypto buyers and traders, and African diaspora users sending money home
problem: Nigerians had difficulty buying and selling cryptocurrency with naira, and diaspora users needed cheap ways to send money home.
business_model: Exchange spread and fees on crypto trades, plus remittance fees via Sendcash

founders.name: Ire Aderinokun
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page. Techpoint (2025-02-11) says her director appointment ended June 30, 2023.

founders.name: Timi Ajiboye
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page. Techpoint says he is the only remaining founder and announced full time work at The Browser Company on 2025-02-03.

founders.name: Olatomiwa Lasebikan
founders.background_notes: Named as founder by Techpoint; his director appointment was terminated in 2021. Not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A naira to crypto exchange needs custody, payments rails and compliance, which are standard but operationally difficult in Nigeria.

defensibility.rationale: Exchange liquidity and trust matter, but several exchanges served Nigerians and users could switch easily.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying by incumbents is sourced. The largest shock was regulatory: the Central Bank of Nigeria 2021 directive barring banks from serving crypto firms, per TechCabal (2025).

market_need_then: No dated 2018 sources on demand were opened. Later coverage (TechCabal 2021) describes the company growing from a peer to peer bitcoin trading site.

branding.name_origin: Techpoint says the company started as Bitkoin in 2017 and renamed to Buycoins after YC acceptance in 2018. Helicarrier announced in October 2021 because the old name did not telegraph its wider products; the company says a thread explains the Helicarrier name, not read.

rebrands.why: Renamed after YC acceptance per Techpoint
Old name did not reflect products beyond buying coins, per the CEO announcement as reported by TechAwkNG

brand_strength.rationale: Buycoins was a recognized Nigerian crypto brand in trade press, but the parent rename to Helicarrier came as the exchange was struggling and no sourced evidence of virality exists.

pivots.to: Helicarrier holding multiple products (Sendcash, Sendcash Pay, NGNT)
pivots.why: Expansion beyond buying coins, per rebrand announcement as reported by TechAwkNG

outcome_analysis: Buycoins grew as a Nigerian crypto exchange after YC Summer 2018 and rebranded to Helicarrier in October 2021 to cover Sendcash, Sendcash Pay and a naira token. The Central Bank of Nigeria 2021 directive on banks and crypto, plus low trading volume, preceded the shutdown of Buycoins Pro (reported January 2024). By February 2025 Techpoint reported that most co-founders had left, with Ajiboye the only one remaining, while the company stayed listed as active.
notes: Status stays Active per YC and Techpoint; it shut Buycoins Pro, not the whole company. The company website helicarrier.studio returned 404 on fetch. Funding: only Microtraction 2018, amount undisclosed (Techpoint); aggregator figures of $1M to $2M are conflicting and unverified, so not recorded as rounds. TechCabal and Medium rebrand posts returned 403 and could not be read. Competitors: Luno and Quidax appear only in 2021 or later ranking articles, so none are listed. Failure factors reflect partial setbacks, not a full shutdown.
